baseline_note: 1509ms from task spec (NN only, sequential numpy, 1024 batch). Our local V0 benchmark measured 555ms; difference likely due to environment/thread-pool differences.
e2e_reference_note: Reference T188v2 total = 549ms features + 84ms LGB + 1509ms NN = 2142ms. T188v3 = 549ms + 84ms + 8ms = 641ms. True speedup ~3.3x.
estimated_note: Based on 2142ms vs 641ms per 1024-batch, 432 batches for 442k rows
implementation: All 50 NNs stacked into (50, out, in) weight tensors; single torch.bmm per layer replaces 50-iteration numpy loop. Per-NN layer norm applied via manual mean/var. CUDA auto-detected at init, falls back to CPU.
note: V1 batched numpy is SLOWER than sequential (0.74x) — batched np.matmul with (50,1024,359) tensors has higher memory allocation overhead than 50 sequential (1024,359) matmuls. V2 torch CPU 3.57x faster (MKL BLAS). V3 torch CUDA 68.5x faster NN-only, 5.46x end-to-end.
